text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV: elevated TLS handshake errors observed for hosted-api (api.redwood.com) in us-east-1. 5m error ratio ~30%. Paging eng-sre on-call.

mike: I'm the on-call. joining. what symptoms are we seeing? user reports of 524/525 and some immediate connection drops?

aditya: yes. front proxy (envoy) logs show a flood of TLS failures starting ~09:04 UTC. sample lines below. Customers hitting us-east see increased failures; routing fallback to us-west started as a quick mitigation.

elaine: quick timeline to collect:
- 09:01 UTC: vendor pushed new VPN tunnel config for gw-us-east-1 (cron window).
- 09:02 UTC: internal change to tunnel set MTU=1400 (was 1500).
- 09:04 UTC: scheduled cert rotation job kicked off for edge certs in us-east.
- 09:06 UTC: monitoring fired for spike in TLS handshake failures. automatic page to eng-sre.
- 09:08 UTC: support begins receiving customer reports.

ben: deploy-bot shows cert-rotation job completed without job-level errors at 09:04:55 UTC (job cr-us-east-20260412). But node-level anomalies possible.

deploy-bot: cert-rotation/us-east: COMPLETED 09:04:55 id=cr-us-east-20260412 logref=alpha

aditya: envoy excerpt (collected 09:05-09:07):
```
[09:05:12] error TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: handshake failure
[09:05:12] error proxy: sni api.redwood.com: no cert available for context
[09:05:13] warn TLS verify: unsupported critical extension in certificate
```

mike: "no cert available" + "unsupported critical extension" implies two different failure modes: (A) some nodes not serving certs at all; (B) certs present but something about the certs or chain isn't acceptable to the proxy/verify. Need to check filesystem and the cert job steps.

ops-bot: network telemetry shows an uptick in ICMP fragmentation and PMTU fallback messages between our gw-us-east-1 and the LB cluster starting 09:02. Attaching a tcpdump snippet.

aditya: tcpdump sample shows large ClientHello getting split into multiple IP fragments (SYN with payload fragments):
```
09:03:58.987654 IP 10.10.5.23.52345 > 10.10.8.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, length 0
09:03:58.987655 IP (frag 1) 10.10.5.23 > 10.10.8.12: frag 1400
09:03:58.987656 IP (frag 2) 10.10.5.23 > 10.10.8.12: frag 700
// full ClientHello spans fragments; many TLS terminators/operators drop fragmented ClientHello
```

ben: that points to PMTU/MTU change causing fragmentation. If ClientHello fragments, some TLS stacks won't reassemble and handshake fails before we can see SNI/cert exchange. Combine that with any nodes missing certs and impact increases.

elaine: I pulled the VPN change request: vendor applied tunnel MTU 1400 during maintenance window at 09:02 (intended to avoid fragmentation on path to DC). That was an unintended value given our internal expectations of 1500.

mike: check target nodes for cert presence. list /etc/ssl/active.pem across the lb fleet. Also confirm if cert rotation used atomic rename or symlink update.

aditya: checking nodes now. result: 4/16 LB nodes show missing /etc/ssl/active.pem (symlink broken), 12/16 have the rotated cert. On the 4 nodes with missing symlink, envoy logs show immediate "no peer cert" and openssl s_client returns no peer certificate.

aditya: example openssl run to an affected node:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.10.8.12:443 -servername api.redwood.com
CONNECTED(00000003)
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
no peer certificate
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 512 bytes
```

ben: investigating cert rotation job: it wrote new certs to /var/lib/cert-rotation/tmp/* then attempted to symlink /etc/ssl/active.pem -> /var/lib/cert-rotation/current.pem. There's a small race where systemd envoy reload fires before symlink fully in place if the restart happens concurrently. Job logs show restarts triggered in parallel on hosts and a handful had reorder; looks like non-atomic swap.

mike: good find. So likely two independent failures: non-atomic cert rotation left a few nodes with no cert; PMTU change induced fragmentation causing many handshakes to fail even to nodes with correct certs. Hypothesis: composite failure. Let's track formally.

aditya: hypothesis tracker:
- H1: non-atomic cert rotation left 4 LBs without a valid active cert symlink -> those nodes returned no cert. Evidence: file checks and openssl.
- H2: tunnel MTU reduction to 1400 fragmented ClientHello -> increased handshake drops across nodes. Evidence: tcpdump, reproduction of handshake failure when forcing MTU=1400.
- H3: malformed certs / unknown critical extension introduced by rotation -> less likely (only seen as transient log lines), certs validated ok on healthy nodes.

mike: reproduction attempt: from test pod, force path MTU to 1400 via ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400 and curl https://api.redwood.com works intermittently; packet captures show ClientHello fragmentation and handshake failures. With MTU 1500 it succeeds consistently. So H2 reproduces.

sara: on remediation: I can push a quick hotfix to the 4 affected LBs: restore pre-rotation cert bundle and restart envoy. Meanwhile netops can revert the tunnel MTU. Which order is preferable? rolling back MTU first may immediately reduce failure volume while we fix certs.

netops-bot: initiating rollback of tunnel MTU to 1500 for gw-us-east-1. change start 09:20, ETA 09:25.

aditya: applying manual cert restore on 4 nodes now (commands run):
```
sudo cp /var/backups/certs/pre-rot/api_redwood.pem /etc/ssl/certs/api_redwood.pem
sudo ln -sf /etc/ssl/certs/api_redwood.pem /etc/ssl/active.pem
sudo systemctl restart envoy
```

mike: netops reports MTU rollback completed 09:24. Observed TLS error rate drop from ~30% -> 4% by 09:27. After cert restore on 4 nodes error rate dropped to ~1.5% by 09:29. Rolling back region routing to us-west at 09:30.

elaine: customer impact summary (initial): the window of elevated failures ~09:04-09:24 UTC; estimated ~6% of requests to us-east affected, with higher failure rates for some ISPs whose DNS cached old entries. Support notified impacted customers at 09:40 UTC.

ben: commander summary of live mitigations:
- netops rolled tunnel MTU back to 1500 (09:24).
- certs restored on 4 LB nodes (09:21-09:23).
- traffic temporarily routed to us-west for primary load (09:08-09:30).
- monitoring and on-call observed stabilization; incident remains open for RCA.

mike: I'm handing off monitoring to sara at 10:15 UTC. Sara, please own the RCA: gather node lists, full deploy logs, tcpdumps, and produce a timeline. Priority follow-ups: make cert rotation atomic; add post-rotation smoke checks; add PMTU/fragmentation alerts for peering; coordinate with vendor to prevent unexpected MTU changes during critical rollouts.

sara: taking it. immediate action items I'll own:
- RCA doc draft (include logs, packet traces, reproducer).
- Implement atomic rotate for cert job (write to new dir + atomic mv).
- Add openssl s_client smoke test as job postcondition across a sample of LBs.
- Add fragmentation/PMTU alert (threshold 0.5% frag rate in 5m).

aditya: additional mitigation ideas: add deployment gating that blocks cert rotation if PMTU or peering changes detected within same maintenance window. And lower DNS TTL for edge endpoints during rollouts so fallback routing takes effect faster.

pagerduty-bot: incident acknowledged and resolved for on-call (mike). Follow-ups created: TASK-5009 (RCA), TASK-5010 (atomic cert rotation), TASK-5011 (PMTU monitoring), TASK-5012 (cert rotation smoke tests).

mike: final assessment: both H1 and H2 contributed. Cert rotation bug affected a small subset of nodes; MTU reduction amplified the outage by fragmenting ClientHello packets and increasing handshake drops across fleet. Root cause: composite (non-atomic cert swap + unexpected tunnel MTU change).

sara: will circulate draft RCA by EOD with timeline and remediation owners. tagging @customer-success to prepare post-incident comms.

incident-bot: incident annotated: mitigations applied and service stable. Incident remains open until RCA doc completed and follow-up tasks closed.

[thread closed for live ops; RCA to be published to docs/incidents/1937654321-rca.md]
